radiology_report:
OLVG Amsterdam Radiology | 15 Jan 2025 | Study: mpMRI prostate

Clinical Indication:
A 54-year-old gentleman presents with a climbing PSA curve (current 5.9 ng/mL) and a previous negative TRUS biopsy, prompting re-evaluation for occult malignancy.

FINDINGS:
The prostate gland measures 44.0 mL and exhibits asymmetry. A discrete abnormality occupies the right peripheral zone at the mid-gland level, spanning roughly 12 x 9 mm. T2-weighted sequences show pronounced hypointensity within this focus. Diffusion-weighted imaging confirms restricted water movement with correspondingly low ADC values. Dynamic contrast-enhanced phases demonstrate early, focal enhancement compared to adjacent tissue. There is no extraprostatic extension, seminal vesicle invasion, or suspicious pelvic lymphadenopathy. The bladder wall and rectal mucosa appear normal.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 5 lesion in the right mid peripheral zone. Prostate volume 44.0 mL yielding a PSA density of 0.14 ng/mL/mL. csPCa predicted probability 0.7418201.

previous_notes.author: Dr. T. Hendriks (GP)
previous_notes.text: Initial workup followed a PSA elevation to 3.9 ng/mL during May 2022. A subsequent climb to 5.2 ng/mL led to a systematic TRUS biopsy in late 2023, which returned entirely negative for malignancy. With PSA values remaining elevated and mild urinary complaints persisting, a urological re-evaluation was scheduled for further imaging and potential repeat sampling.
